text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on September 15 in history.
1789 - The U.S. Department of Foreign Affairs, created in 1781, changed its name to the Department of State.
1830 - Porfirio Diaz, Mexican statesman, born. He was president from 1877 until 1911 when Francisco Madero's revolution forced him to resign and flee into exile.
1857 - William Howard Taft, 27th U.S. president (1909-13), born.

1859 - Isambard Kingdom Brunel, British engineer of railways, steamships and docks, died. Designer of the first transatlantic steamer, the "Great Western", and the "Great Eastern", until 1899 the largest vessel ever built.
1864 - John Speke, English explorer in Africa, the first European to reach Lake Victoria, died when he accidentally shot himself while partridge shooting.
1879 - Sir Joseph Aloysius Lyons, Australian statesman, born. Helped form the United Australia Party in 1931, and was prime minister 1931-39.

1890 - Dame Agatha Christie, English novelist, born. Known for her popular mystery novels, she created the crime-solving characters of Belgian detective Hercule Poirot and eccentric spinster Miss Jane Marple. In February 1996, her murder mystery "The Mousetrap", the world's longest-running play, passed a theatrical milestone with its 18,000th performance.
1904 - Umberto II of Italy born. Became king in May 1946, but abdicated a month later when Italy voted to become a republic.
1907 - Fay Wray, U.S. film actress, born. Best remembered for her role in "King Kong" as the frightened girl carried to the top of the Empire State Building in New York by an infatuated gorilla.
1916 - Military tanks, originated by Sir Ernest Swinton, were first sent into action as part of the allied offensive at the Battle of the Somme.

1935 - In Germany, the Nazis enacted the Nuremburg Laws, starting off a programme of violent religious and racial persecution. All Jews were deprived of their citizenship, ghettos were revived and the Swastika became the national flag.
1935 - Manuel Luis Quezon was elected first president of the Philippine Commonwealth.
1949 - Konrad Adenauer was elected first chancellor of West Germany and Theodor Heuss first president.
1950 - In the Korean War, the U.N. landing at Inchon proved decisive in the defeat of North Korean troops.

1972 - Two former White House aides, Howard Hunt and Gordon Liddy, were added to the five men already charged with the June 17 break-in and alleged bugging of the Democratic Party headquarters in the Watergate building.
1973 - King Gustav VI Adolf of Sweden died aged 90 and was succeeded by his grandson Carl XVI Gustav.
1978 - Wilhelm Messerschmitt, German aircraft designer and manufacturer, died. In 1944 his Me 262 became the first jet plane to be flown in combat.
1983 - Israeli Prime Minister Menachim Begin, founder of the right-wing Likud party, resigned, to be replaced by Yitzhak Shamir.
1994 - Chechen leader Dzhokhar Dudayev signed a decree imposing martial law and a curfew in the breakaway Russian republic.
1994 - The U.S. flag was lowered over the U.S. liaison office in Somalia and the last marine guards left in a low-key final act to 21 months of American intervention.
